## p180 A3 — Enemy follows withdrawal near Giurgiu; Braila and Focsani evacuated

**Edition context:** p180 A — Enemy following the withdrawal near Giurgiu.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p180-a-p180-a--enemy-following-the-withdrawal-near-giurgiu"></a>


[Source and certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/README.md)

**Record:** the surviving third part of message A on printed p180.
**Result:** the published Nov10–12 key fixes 77 of 78 raw plaintext positions.
A coherent 78-character edition needs nine known-coordinate substitutions
and one printed-dash fill. The source date remains uncertain.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p180-a-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Bei Giurgiu folgt Feind langsam. Braila, Focsani geraeumt.
> 11. Armee keine Ereignisse. OKM.

**Meaning:** The enemy follows slowly near Giurgiu; Braila and Focsani have
been evacuated. No events are reported for the 11th Army.

The second `1` in the proposed army number is an explicit repair to the
already known `1` square cell. It does not assign a duplicate `1` to an
unresolved cell. The other parts of this report have not been supplied.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p180-a-raw-decipherment-and-edition"></a>

contains 156 slots, agreeing with `RICHI-156`. Source-visible coordinates
misread by OCR were restored before analysis; the sole printed dash is
retained as an erasure in the raw record.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p180-a-source-and-credit"></a>

### Source and credit

Printed p180 / PDF page 183, `A) --- v ZON`, with an uncertain handwritten date,
and `3 TL RICHI-156`. This edition does not infer an exact day from the key
period. The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

## p180 B2 — Romanian mobilization and a crossing report

**Edition context:** 11 November: Romanian mobilization and a crossing report.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov11-romanian-mobilization-report-november-11-romanian-mobilization-and-a-crossing-report"></a>



The surviving second part on printed page 180 reports mobilization and a crossing. Its last line is followed by **“(jammed to end)”**. The source contains **235 printed slots**, including two dashes, under a **RICHI-240** header. Keeping every printed slot and appending five unknown coordinates produces a conditional 240-coordinate frame with **110 of 120 plaintext positions fixed** under the unchanged published Nov10–12 key.

Six narrow word proposals raise that count to **116 of 120**. They cost **four observed-coordinate substitutions, one printed-mask fill and four fills of added tail slots**. The remaining source dash, first added tail slot and two linked occurrences of an unknown square cell stay unresolved. Date-like fields, the shortened **KRIEGSZUSAND** and the literal **ZIMNICA** are preserved. This is a partial source edition of one surviving part; the absent first part and a unique original transmission are not reconstructed.

Research and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The period key is credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, with its publication details retained in [inputs.json](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/inputs.json). Earlier local native and terminal-mask trials already exposed this lead. Their transcription and reproducible outputs are retained in [prior_candidates.json](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/prior_candidates.json); this edition does not claim first-decipherment priority.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p180_B2_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/sources/p180_B2_reviewed.png) · [p180_D1_header_comparison.png](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/sources/p180_D1_header_comparison.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).


<a id="source-p180-b2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov11-romanian-mobilization-report-p180-b2"></a>

### p180 B2

Literal header: `B) LP v ZON (0[1/4].02 p.m. November 11th); -----; 2 TL RICHI-240`.

The damaged hour glyph remains ambiguous between `01.02` and `04.02`. The older OCR reads 01.02. An enlarged comparison with the same page’s clear 4 in the D1 header does not decisively exclude either reading. The complete alternatives are `B) LP v ZON (01.02 p.m. November 11th); -----; 2 TL RICHI-240` and `B) LP v ZON (04.02 p.m. November 11th); -----; 2 TL RICHI-240`. Neither is selected by the body’s date or hour fields.

[Printed page 180, B2 and its terminal-jamming note — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/inputs.json)

[The neighboring D1 header used only for glyph comparison — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/inputs.json) is not a second recovered body in this edition.

The printed 2 TL identifies this as a second part. No first-part body is present under this reception header on page 180. All five-character groups remain intact and in order; the final line has seven groups. Source dashes occupy indices **200 and 201**. All indices in this edition are zero-based.
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov11-romanian-mobilization-report-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The mobilization report gains the order date **9 November** and the linked **9 Uhr abends**, taking the existing edited layer from **116/120 to 118/120**. Decree 3179 is dated 27 October, one day before the poster’s first mobilization day of 28 October / 10 November. Identifying the report’s order with this decree selects the 9 branch. The two remaining masks and all prior source repairs remain explicit. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

The 240-slot model appends unknowns at model indices **235–239**. Every earlier model index maps to the identically numbered printed slot. The five-slot shortfall and the explicit terminal-jamming note motivate this position. They do not prove that an interior loss is impossible, and no exhaustive search for a unique loss geometry is claimed.

The words MOBILMACHUNG, TAG, UHRABENDS and FEIND are already fixed in this frame. Parts of ANGEORDNET and the two place-like sequences need explicit changes or fills. The numerical labels remain outputs of the published partial square, not independently established calendar dates.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov11-romanian-mobilization-report-priced-word-proposal"></a>

### Priced word proposal

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — 4 observed-coordinate substitutions, 1 printed-mask fill and 4 added-tail fills:**

```text
RUMAENXMOBILMACHUNG?X11XANGEORDNETXX1XTAG10X?1LXKRIEGSZUSAND10X1TX?UHRABENDSXFEIND1?X11XTURNUMAGURELEZIMNICAUEBERGESETZT
```

</details>

**Readable German — the complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Rumaen. Mobilmachung ? 11 angeordnet. 1. Tag 10 ?1L. Kriegszusand 10 1T ? Uhr abends. Feind 1? 11 Turnumagurele Zimnica uebergesetzt.

**Conditional interpretation — partial report and unresolved fields:**

The proposed wording concerns Romanian mobilization, an order, a state of war and an enemy crossing. TURNUMAGURELE and ZIMNICA are the exact candidate letter sequences. No modern place spelling is inserted. KRIEGSZUSAND retains the missing T of the resulting stream; replacing it by the standard KRIEGSZUSTAND would add a plaintext position and is outside this frame. The fields following MOBILMACHUNG, TAG, KRIEGSZUSAND and FEIND remain literal, including ? 11, 10 ?1L, 10 1T ? and 1? 11. A specific mobilization date, declaration time or crossing date is not selected.

| Proposed span | Plaintext start | Observed changes | Printed-mask fills | Added-tail fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| RUMAEN | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| ANGEORDNET | 24 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| KRIEGSZUSAND | 48 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| TURNUMAGURELE | 88 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| ZIMNICA | 101 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| UEBERGESETZT | 108 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| **Total** | | **4** | **1** | **4** |

The substitutions within A1GEORDNET and MAGUR2 replace the literal raw labels 1 and 2 only in those disclosed word proposals. The separate number/date fields are unchanged. The precise coordinate ledger is:

| Model index | Printed source index | Before | After | Cost class |
| ---: | ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |

There are **five added coordinates** in the frame, even though the proposal fills only four. Model index 235 remains unknown. The unchanged source dash at index 200 also remains unknown. No printed coordinate is excluded.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov11-romanian-mobilization-report-coupled-residual-possibilities"></a>

### Coupled residual possibilities

| Plaintext index | Coordinate pair | Exact remaining domain | Coordinate source |
| ---: | :---: | --- | --- |
| 19 | XA | 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 | Printed source 227,77 |
| 44 | ?A | 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, C, L, O | Source dash 200 and printed source 20 |
| 66 | XA | 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 | Printed source 38,113 |
| 83 | ?X | 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, E, N, V, X | Added model slot 235 and printed source 85 |

Positions **19 and 66 use the same unknown square cell** and must have the same label. They cannot independently be assigned different dates or hours. If source dash 200 is completed as X, position 44 also uses that same XA cell. If added slot 235 is completed as X, position 83 uses XX, whose label must differ from XA under a one-to-one square completion.

The verifier checks all **120 assignments** of the five missing square labels and all **36 coordinate completions** of source 200 and model 235: **4,320 exact full re-encryptions**. They yield **270 distinct residual label tuples** at positions 19,44,66,83. One complete witness for every tuple is retained in the certificate. Those additional fills demonstrate the alternatives; none is adopted into the displayed proposal.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-okm-radio-route"></a>

## p180 C — OKM communication route through literal AOK1? and FXT

**Edition context:** OKM availability through an incompletely identified radio route.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-okm-radio-route-okm-availability-through-an-incompletely-identified-radio-route"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This short native body reports a communication route to OKM. Its readable wording is an explicitly priced proposal, while AOK1? and FXT remain literal. The unresolved address character is a source erasure with both numerical and alphabetic possibilities.

<a id="source-p180-c"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-okm-radio-route-p180-c"></a>

### p180 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) LP-vZON (----- November 11th); 24.00; RIZI-86`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ANOHLXOKMXOKMUEBERAOK1?XSUBCHFXTXEHREACHHAR
```

**Edited output — 6 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ANOHLXOKMXOKMUEBERAOK1?XDURCHFXTXERREICHBAR
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> An OHL. OKM. OKM ueber AOK1? durch FXT erreichbar.

**Meaning:** The proposed reading addresses OHL and OKM and reports that OKM can be reached via the literal address AOK1? through FXT. The last address character and FXT are not expanded into a unit identity or named station.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 86 occupied source slots are retained in native order. The O-like glyph in FAXOX is masked and remains unfilled.
- SUBCH to DURCH and EHREACHHAR to ERREICHBAR cost six observed-coordinate substitutions in total. The exact raw layer remains available; the familiar wording is not represented as an unedited source reading.
- The unresolved source position in AOK1? has domain {1, 4, A, R, T, U}. It is not necessarily a numerical digit, and the edition does not choose a standard army designation.
- FXT remains a literal routing label. The missing interception-time field and separate printed 24.00 line are retained without chronological normalization.

### Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

## p180 D1 — Evening report on an unanswered Romanian evacuation ultimatum

**Edition context:** p180 D1 — Evening report on the Romanian evacuation ultimatum.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov11-romanian-ultimatum-report-p180-d1--evening-report-on-the-romanian-evacuation-ultimatum"></a>



**Recovery and source review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Restoring a
mispaired duplicate/missing-group frame exposes this evening report to OHL.
The reconstructed 98-position body reports an unanswered Romanian ultimatum
and preserves `24 STUNDEN VOR DER WAFFENSTRECKUNG` literally.

<a id="source-p180-d1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov11-romanian-ultimatum-report-p180-d1"></a>

### p180 D1

**Readable German — conditional 196-slot reconstruction; six observed-source exclusions, five added-slot fills, ten printed-mask fills and two observed substitutions:**

> An OHL. Abendmeldung. Rumaen. Ultimatum forderte Raeumung 24 Stunden vor der Waffenstreckung. Nicht beantwortet.

An evening report to OHL concerns a Romanian ultimatum demanding evacuation
and says it was not answered. `24 Stunden vor der Waffenstreckung` is the
literal time phrase; the edition does not turn it into a calendar deadline.
`Rumaen.` displays the transmitted abbreviation `RUMAEN` without adding
letters. The related [p175 report](175.md#edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions) concerns
an ultimatum too, but supplies no copied text or coordinates here.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — primary conditional 196-slot frame, before all substitutions and fills; 85/98 fixed labels:**

```text
ANOHLX?BE?DME??UN?XRU?AENXULT?MATUMFO?D2RTERAEUM?NG24STUNDENVORDERWAFFENSTRECKUN?XNICHTB?ANTW?RT?T
```

</details>

The manuscript prints **197 slots**, against `RICHI-196`: 187 observed
coordinates, nine dashes and one invalid `O`-like glyph. The two `XGVXD` groups
at source 125 and 130 are genuinely repeated, as are the final `A` positions
195 and 196. The primary frame excludes one duplicated group and one final
`A`, then inserts five unknown coordinates before original source 150.
All original glyphs remain in the source transcription below.

| Minimum-frame choice | Fixed raw labels | Five inserted values in the complete candidate |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Gap before original source 150, retained-stream boundary 145 | 85/98 | `DXXDD` |
| Gap before original source 151, retained-stream boundary 146 | 84/98 | `XXDDD` |

Both gap geometries combine with two duplicate-group origins and two final-A
origins: **eight tied source maps**, all yielding the same completed
ciphertext. Two independent encoders compare all **768** maps in this stated
family against the fixed lexical proposal. The two-substitution minimum
prices that proposal within this family.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same primary frame; two observed substitutions, ten printed-mask fills and five inserted-slot fills; 98/98 fixed labels:**

```text
ANOHLXABENDMELDUNGXRUMAENXULTIMATUMFORDERTERAEUMUNG24STUNDENVORDERWAFFENSTRECKUNGXNICHTBEANTWORTET
```

</details>

Only source **40 V→X** and **121 X→D** change observed coordinates. These
restore the `E` of `FORDERTE` and the `O` of `BEANTWORTET`; the latter is an
observed-coordinate change even though its earlier square cell was unknown.
The ten printed masks and five added slots receive separate fill ledgers.
The literal `24`, the negative `NICHT`, the published key and all other
observed coordinates survive unchanged. The raw ending already preserves
`VOR DER WAFFENSTRECKUN? X NICHT B?ANTW?RT?T`.

## p180 E — Bauman readiness and Cassel transport

**Edition context:** Namur arrival, Cassel transport and armistice-information requests.

**Related source pages:** [p172 C1](172.md#source-p172-c1), [p172 C3](172.md#source-p172-c3), [p181 B](181.md#source-p181-b).

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-namur-arrival-cassel-transport-and-armistice-information-requests"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four surviving source bodies report an arrival at Namur, direct prompt transport arrangements to Cassel, and request the local armistice conditions again. The Namur telegram explicitly lacks its second part; its first and third parts are presented without bridging that gap. Literal office labels, an opaque transport field and source-length spellings remain visible.

<a id="source-p180-e"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-p180-e"></a>

### p180 E

**Source transcription — header:** `E) SY A v SY (10.09 p.m., November 12th); 10.45; RICHI-224`

**Readable German:** based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Lt. Bauman. STATON sofort marschbereit 0 sein fuer M?TRANSPORT Cassel. Abtransport so schnell wie moeglich regeln. Kommandeur.

**Meaning:** The instruction addresses Lt. Bauman, calls for immediate readiness to move, and directs transport to Cassel to be arranged as quickly as possible. The spelling STATON and the literal fields 0 and M? TRANSPORT remain unresolved; the specific transport type is not identified.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBERECT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELSWIEMOEGLICHRE?ELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBEREIT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELLWIEMOEGLICHREGELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source contains 224 slots, including all final groups; no coordinate is inserted, removed or moved.
- STATON is retained without inserting the absent I of STATION. BAUMAN remains the literal surname with one terminal N.
- MARSCHBERECT0 to MARSCHBEREIT0, SCHNELS to SCHNELL and RE?ELN to REGELN are separately priced lexical changes. The literal 0 is not silently changed into a separator.
- The Nov13–15b published key is used because it yields the demonstrated reading; the printed 12 November date is retained as a different evidence layer.
- The unknown position in M?TRANSPORT comes from an unresolved square cell and remains globally coupled. Its label is not chosen from historical expectations.

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical round-trip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

### p172 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) SY v ZM (13.40 p.m., November 10th); 1412 3 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-116`

**Readable German:** based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Major Kroeger. GHQU. Soeben mit RXABLASS Namur eingetroffen.

**Meaning:** The first surviving part names Major Kroeger and reports a recent arrival at Namur. The opening may address Kroeger, so the arriving person is not securely identified. GHQU and RXABLASS remain opaque labels. The surviving third part closes with Hpt. Mannstaedt, and the source explicitly marks part 2 as missing.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXIOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

**Edited output** — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXSOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The native 116-slot first part is complete. The source explicitly prints “2 TL (Missing)” before the separately preserved third part; no second part is supplied or counted.
- IOEBEN to SOEBEN is an explicitly priced lexical proposal. GHQU and RXABLASS remain literal and unexpanded; ABLASS is not asserted to be a person's name. The opening could be an address, and no arriving subject is supplied.
- The printed time is 13.40 p.m. and is retained without conversion. No historical identity beyond the literal surname KROEGER is inferred.

### p181 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) LP v NKJ (01.00 a.m., November 12th); 23.10 (12/11); RICHI-234`

**Readable German:** based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> An OHL. OKM und AOK11. Erbitten nochmals Mitteilung der besonderen Waffenstillstandsbedingungen fuer hiesigen Kriegsschauplatz.

**Meaning:** The sender again asks OHL, OKM and the literal addressee AOK11 for the specific armistice conditions applying to the local theater of operations. The text is a request for information, not the conditions themselves.


**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- Both header times and the separate 12/11 line remain literal. The label AOK11 is not used to prove a historical unit identification.
